briefings.title: 2026 Lemley Lecture Featuring AI Pioneer Yann LeCun
briefings.tldr: Yann LeCun argues that current Large Language Models (LLMs) will never achieve human-level intelligence; instead, the future of AI lies in "World Models" that use Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) to understand physical reality and perform hierarchical planning.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Yann LeCun argues that current Large Language Models (LLMs) will never achieve human-level intelligence; instead, the future of AI lies in "World Models" that use Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) to understand physical reality and perform hierarchical planning.

## The Failure of the LLM Paradigm
- **Data Inefficiency:** Language data is insufficient for human-level intelligence.
  - LLMs are trained on roughly $10^{14}$ bytes of text, representing 400,000 years of reading.
  - A four-year-old child has processed $10^{14}$ bytes of visual data in just 16,000 hours of wake time.
- **Moravec’s Paradox:** AI can pass the bar exam but cannot perform basic physical tasks, such as clearing a dinner table or driving a car with the efficiency of a teenager (20 hours of practice).
- **The "Agentic" Flaw:** Current systems are not truly agentic because they cannot predict the consequences of their actions.
  - Scaling LLMs to reach human-level intelligence is described by LeCun as "complete BS."
  - Autoregressive token prediction is computationally inferior to inference via search and optimization.

## World Models and JEPA Architectures
- **Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA):** LeCun proposes moving away from generative models (which try to predict every pixel) toward joint embedding.
  - **Abstract Representations:** JEPAs predict the "state" of the world in an abstract space, ignoring unpredictable details (like the exact texture of a wall) to focus on relevant outcomes.
  - **Non-Collapsing Systems:** Tools like **SigReg** (developed with Brown faculty Randall Balestriero) help maximize information content and prevent the system from "collapsing" into useless, constant representations.
- **Hierarchical Planning:** Human intelligence relies on decomposing goals.
  - A trip from NYU to Paris involves subgoals (getting to the airport) and lower-level actions (hailing a taxi, walking).
  - Current AI cannot yet perform this type of multi-level planning; it remains a primary research frontier.
- **Inherent Safety:** Systems built on world models are intrinsically safer because they can use "guardrail objectives" during the planning phase to reject actions with dangerous predicted outcomes.

## Industry Impact and the Future of Ami Labs
- **Industrial Applications:** The first successful world models will likely operate "behind the curtain" in B2B sectors.
  - **Use Cases:** Optimizing jet engines, refineries, chemical plants, and drug production by predicting system states via thousands of sensors.
  - **Scientific Discovery:** AI can learn "phenomenological models" for complex systems that defy simple reductionist equations, such as discovering materials for more efficient catalysis or higher refractive indices.
- **The Open Source Advantage:** LeCun's new company, **Ami Labs**, intends to follow the open research model established at Meta’s FAIR.
  - Open source allows for "exploratory research" through resident PhD students and academic collaboration, which LeCun credits for the success of models like Llama.

## Guidance for Education and Career
- **Focus on Fundamentals:** Students should prioritize subjects with a long "shelf life."
  - **Core Recommendation:** Given a choice between mobile app programming and quantum mechanics, choose quantum mechanics.
  - Fundamental physics and math provide the framework for learning new technologies as they emerge.
- **Learning to Learn:** As technological progress accelerates, the ability to adapt to new situatons "zero-shot" is the ultimate competitive advantage for both humans and machines.

## Notable Quotes
> "The people who think that by training LLMs and making them bigger... we're going to reach human intelligence are deluded. It's complete BS." - on the current AI investment bubble.

> "Intelligence is the ability to accomplish new tasks you've never been exposed to and solve new problems without any prior training... fast adaptation in front of new situations." - on the definition of true AI.

> "The most incomprehensible thing about the world is that the world is comprehensible." - quoting Albert Einstein on the power of abstract modeling.

> "Abandon generative models... abandon reinforcement learning. Minimize its use because it's so damn inefficient." - on the necessary shifts in AI research.

briefings.title: How Bots, Deepfakes and AI Agents Are Forcing a New Internet Identity Layer | Alex Blania on a16z

people.name: Alex Blania
people.role: Cofounder and CEO, Tools for Humanity and World

briefings.tldr: As AI agents and deepfakes become indistinguishable from humans, World (formerly Worldcoin) is establishing a global identity layer using iris biometrics and privacy-preserving cryptography to verify "proof of human" uniqueness without compromising individual anonymity.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
As AI agents and deepfakes become indistinguishable from humans, World (formerly Worldcoin) is establishing a global identity layer using iris biometrics and privacy-preserving cryptography to verify "proof of human" uniqueness without compromising individual anonymity.

## The Identity Crisis: Why Current Proofs are Failing
The rapid evolution of AI has rendered traditional methods of verifying human identity on the internet obsolete.

*   **Failure of Digital-Only Proofs:** Methods like "Web of Trust" (analyzing social graphs or GitHub history) are no longer viable because AI can maintain long-term accounts, post regularly, and even vouch for other AI agents.
*   **The Uniqueness Problem:** Proof of human is a "1-to-N" problem (distinguishing one person from billions of others), whereas FaceID is a "1-to-1" problem (verifying you are the same person who owns the phone). 
*   **Mathematical Entropy:** Common biometrics like fingerprints or facial recognition lack the mathematical complexity to distinguish individuals at a global scale. The iris is the only biometric with enough "entropy" to solve the uniqueness problem for billions of users.
*   **AI Superiority in Persuasion:** AI is becoming "superhuman" at programming humans. Blania cites studies where AI outperformed humans in changing minds on subreddits by analyzing user profiles to tailor psychological triggers.

## Technical Architecture: The Orb and Privacy
To solve the privacy-vs-verification paradox, World utilizes custom hardware and advanced cryptography.

*   **The Orb:** A custom hardware device designed to prevent "replay attacks." It uses multiple sensors across the electromagnetic spectrum to ensure it is scanning a real, living human rather than a high-resolution display or deepfake.
*   **Multi-Party Computation (MPC):** To avoid a central database of biometric data, World splits iris codes into multiple pieces stored across different computers. No single entity possesses the full biometric "key."
*   **Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKP):** Users hold a secret on their phone that proves they are part of the verified uniqueness set without revealing who they are. This allows for fully anonymous authentication on third-party platforms.
*   **Authentication Levels:** 
    *   **High-Level:** Iris verification via the Orb.
    *   **Mid-Level:** Face checks via smartphone (useful for rate-limiting but vulnerable to advanced deepfakes).
    *   **Legacy:** Government ID integration using NFC chips, though this is less popular due to privacy stigmas.

## Immediate Use Cases for Human Verification
The need for proof of personhood extends beyond social media bots to any high-stakes human interaction.

*   **Dating and Social Media:** Tinder is testing World ID in Japan to issue badges that signal high-level verification, ensuring users are not interacting with "catfish" bots.
*   **Video Conferencing:** As real-time deepfakes become photorealistic, high-value users (e.g., fund managers) will need cryptographic proof that the person on a video call is who they claim to be to prevent fraudulent wire transfers.
*   **Gaming:** Verifying human players is critical to preventing AI from destroying competitive integrity or economy-based betting markets.
*   **Advertising Integrity:** Content platforms like YouTube need to distinguish between human viewers and "YouTube farms" (thousands of phones watching videos) to maintain the value of ad impressions.

## Scaling and Go-to-Market Strategy
The primary challenge for World is the physical distribution of hardware to reach a global audience.

*   **The 15-Minute Target:** Blania’s goal is to reduce the "average minutes to reach a device" to under 15 minutes globally. In the U.S., this requires deploying approximately 50,000 Orbs.
*   **Distribution Partnerships:** The company is exploring large-scale partnerships with retailers (e.g., Walmart or Starbucks) and even government entities like the DMV.
*   **Orb-on-Demand:** A new service is launching in the Bay Area where Orbs are delivered via motorbike to a user’s location for immediate verification, reducing the friction of finding a static location.

## Notable Quotes

> "The AIs are really good at programming humans. Much better than humans are at programming AIs. Absolutely. No question." — **Alex Blania**

> "An AI will be able to have a GitHub account and will be able to post and also attest to five other AIs that these are in fact humans even though they're not." — **Alex Blania**

> "What we currently see [with bots and deepfakes] is less than 1% of what it will look like in probably a year or two." — **Alex Blania**

> "To solve the proof of human problem, you will need to distinguish one new individual from all previous individuals... you find out that things like face or fingerprints don't work. You end up with something like the iris, which has enough entropy." — **Alex Blania**

briefings.title: Jack Dorsey: Every Company Can Now Be a Mini-AGI
briefings.tldr: Jack Dorsey is transitioning Block from a traditional corporate hierarchy to a centralized AI "intelligence layer," reducing the workforce by 40% to eliminate "lossy" human management chains and refocusing the human role on high-level judgment, taste, and creative alignment.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Jack Dorsey is transitioning Block from a traditional corporate hierarchy to a centralized AI "intelligence layer," reducing the workforce by 40% to eliminate "lossy" human management chains and refocusing the human role on high-level judgment, taste, and creative alignment.

## The Shift: From Hierarchy to "Mini-AGI"
*   **Information Legibility:** Dorsey argues that traditional hierarchies exist primarily to manage information flow, which is inherently slow and "lossy." By capturing all digital artifacts (code, Slack, docs) into an intelligence layer, the company becomes a "world model" or "mini-AGI" that any employee or board member can query in real time.
*   **The "Circle" Model:** Unlike the "Pyramid" (Manager Mode) or "Flat" (Founder Mode), Dorsey proposes a circle with AI at the center and humans at the edge. The system provides the ground truth, while humans provide alignment and course correction.
*   **Eliminating the Roadmap:** Dorsey believes a company’s ultimate limiting factor is its fixed roadmap. In the new model, customer queries and proactive intelligence determine what is built in real time, shifting the company from "navigational interfaces" to "conversational capabilities."

## Reimagining Organizational Roles
Block is normalizing its 6,000-person workforce into just three distinct roles to increase velocity and decrease organizational depth (aiming for 2-3 layers max):
*   **Individual Contributor (IC):** The builders and operators (engineers, designers, sales) who use AI agents to augment their breadth, allowing one person to do the work previously requiring a team of ten.
*   **Directly Responsible Individual (DRI):** The owners of customer outcomes who set strategy, assemble IC teams, and take full accountability for success or failure.
*   **Player Coach:** Replacing traditional managers, these individuals build human capacity and mastery. They do not just "tell" but "show" by doing the work alongside their teams.
*   **CEO Mandate:** The CEO's role shifts from decision-making to "architecting the intelligence" and ensuring the "edge" of humans remains aligned with the company’s values and "taste."

## Executing the 40% Workforce Reduction
*   **The Catalyst:** The decision followed the late 2023/early 2024 release of advanced AI tools like **Goose** (a coding agent harness) and **Cloud Code**, which proved capable of understanding large, legacy codebases.
*   **The "Shit Sandwich" Strategy:** Dorsey and his team decided to execute a massive cut (40%) from a position of strength rather than reacting to market weakness. 
*   **The Math of Excellence:** The team calculated the absolute minimum number of people required for three pillars:
    1.  Maintaining 100% uptime.
    2.  Full regulatory and legal compliance.
    3.  Growth and the transition to an AI-native structure.
*   **Board Transparency:** Roelof Botha noted the decision was supported because it was "principled and logical" rather than reactionary. Dorsey provided a detailed, logic-based manifesto to build trust before execution.

## Leadership and Board Dynamics
*   **The ALE Framework:** Roelof Botha defines timeless CEO qualities through the acronym **ALE**: **A**uthenticity, **L**ogic, and **E**mpathy. 
*   **Board Selection:** Dorsey advises founders to treat investor selection as a "hire you can never fire." He suggests bringing in independent board members early (after product-market fit) to provide mentorship and a buffer between the founder and VCs.
*   **Avoid the "Anti-Pattern":** Dorsey strongly warns against being the CEO of two public companies simultaneously, calling it an "anti-goal" that leads to over-delegation and the accidental creation of disconnected holding companies.
*   **Meditation as Training:** Dorsey views meditation not as a "woo-woo" practice, but as physical training to sharpen focus, observe without reacting, and recognize the impermanence of business crises.

## Notable Quotes
> "Traditionally we've been relying upon humans in a management structure... to relay information. Instead, we can take all those artifacts and put an intelligence on top of it, build a model around it, and actually have a conversation with the company about how the company is doing." — **Jack Dorsey**

> "It's not somebody who pounds the table harder who gets their product approved, it's just: more customers want this than that. That’s how we’re going to decide what to build next." — **Roelof Botha**

> "If we knew that this was what our company was going to be in the future, I didn't want to have to do it with our backs against the wall... I want to be ahead of it because then we can do it with a lot more integrity and generosity." — **Jack Dorsey**

> "I think AI is the biggest drainer of moats companies have ever seen. But some of the basics of dealing with people and leading remain true." — **Roelof Botha**

briefings.title: LIVE: President Trump addresses nation on Iran 9 ET
briefings.tldr: President Trump declared a decisive military victory one month into "Operation Epic Fury," claiming the near-total destruction of Iran's navy and air force while setting a two-to-three-week timeline to conclude objectives and urging global allies to secure their own energy routes.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump declared a decisive military victory one month into "Operation Epic Fury," claiming the near-total destruction of Iran's navy and air force while setting a two-to-three-week timeline to conclude objectives and urging global allies to secure their own energy routes.

## Military Progress of "Operation Epic Fury"
*   **Current Standing:** One month into the conflict, President Trump asserted that U.S. forces have achieved "swift, decisive, overwhelming victories," claiming Iran's navy is destroyed and its air force is in ruins.
*   **Nuclear and Missile Deterrence:**
    *   **Operation Midnight Hammer:** Trump highlighted previous B-2 bomber strikes on key nuclear facilities, stating those sites are now "dust" and under constant satellite surveillance.
    *   **Capabilities:** Iranian ballistic missile and drone production have been "systematically dismantled," with analysts noting launch frequency has dropped to less than 10% of peak levels.
*   **The "Short-Term" Timeline:** 
    *   The President signaled the mission would be completed "shortly," specifically targeting a two-to-three-week window for final operations.
    *   **Contingency:** If no diplomatic deal is reached, Trump threatened to strike Iran’s entire electrical grid simultaneously.

## Shift in Global Alliances and NATO
*   **NATO Criticism:** Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio criticized the alliance as a "one-way street." Trump labeled NATO a "paper tiger" and "free riders," expressing disgust with members who refuse to designate the IRGC as a terrorist organization or allow the use of U.S. bases.
*   **Middle East Partners:** Trump explicitly thanked Israel, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the UAE, Kuwait, and Bahrain for their support during the operation.
*   **The Venezuela Precedent:** Trump touted the rapid military takeover of Venezuela as a model of success, noting that the U.S. and Venezuela are now "joint venture partners" in oil production.

## Energy Independence and the Strait of Hormuz
*   **U.S. Energy Dominance:** Trump emphasized that because of "drill baby drill" policies, the U.S. is the #1 producer of oil and gas and is "totally independent of the Middle East."
*   **Responsibility Shift:**
    *   Trump told countries dependent on the Strait of Hormuz to "build up some delayed courage" and protect the passage themselves.
    *   **Economic Suggestion:** He encouraged nations struggling with fuel costs to bypass the Middle East and buy oil directly from the United States.
*   **Market Impact:** Analysts Benham Taleblu and Hal Kempfer noted that the speech was designed to "hand-hold" global markets and calm fears of a "forever war," despite rising gas prices at home.

## Post-War Strategy and Expert Analysis
*   **Regime Status:** Trump claimed that while regime change was not the official goal, it has effectively occurred because the original leadership is "all dead," replaced by a "less radical" group.
*   **Strategic Risks:** 
    *   **The "Toll Booth" Problem:** Benham Taleblu (FDD) warned against leaving Iran in control of the Strait of Hormuz, as they may implement a "toll booth" system to tax international commerce.
    *   **Chinese Involvement:** Hal Kempfer expressed concern that a U.S. withdrawal from the Persian Gulf could open the door for increased Chinese naval involvement in the region.
*   **Future Operations:** Experts suggested the "shortly" timeline likely involves specialized raids or "mowing the lawn" strikes rather than a large-scale land occupation.

## Notable Quotes
> "Never in the history of warfare has an enemy suffered such clear and devastating large-scale losses in a matter of weeks. Our enemies are losing and America... is winning bigger than ever before." — **President Donald Trump**

> "I was really asking [for NATO help] because I wanted to see what they’d do. We didn’t need them... I didn’t need NATO stepping in our way because they’re a paper tiger." — **President Donald Trump**

> "If I have to put a nice bow on it, this was an attempt to hand-hold both markets as well as the American public and bring them along and make sure that they understood both the stakes as well as the interests at play." — **Benham Taleblu, Foundation for Defense of Democracies**

> "He’s also trying to calm the markets... [Trump] made it very clear he does not like these long wars that draw our resources away." — **Hal Kempfer, Retired Marine Intelligence Officer**

briefings.title: LIVE: President Trump addresses the nation
briefings.tldr: President Trump declared near-total military victory in the five-week-old war against Iran (Operation Epic Fury), claiming the regime's military is "decimated" and its leadership dead, while warning of 2-3 more weeks of intense strikes to force a final nuclear deal.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump declared near-total military victory in the five-week-old war against Iran (Operation Epic Fury), claiming the regime's military is "decimated" and its leadership dead, while warning of 2-3 more weeks of intense strikes to force a final nuclear deal.

## Military Status and "Operation Epic Fury"
* **Operational Success:** Trump claimed the U.S. has "obliterated" Iran’s Navy and Air Force, destroyed its missile and drone capabilities, and decimated the command and control of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).
    * **Scope of Strikes:** Approximately 13,000 targets have been hit in 32 days of conflict.
    * **Casualties:** 13 U.S. service members have been killed in the operation; approximately 300 have been injured.
* **The "Stone Age" Timeline:** The President signaled a final escalation, stating the military will hit Iran "extremely hard" over the next two to three weeks to "bring them back to the stone ages."
* **Ground Operations:** Despite internal briefings on limited ground force options (such as seizing Kharg Island), the President did not announce a ground invasion, focusing instead on air and missile superiority.
* **Venezuela Mention:** Trump noted a separate "quick, lethal" military action in Venezuela, referring to the country as a "joint venture partner" in oil production following a regime change.

## Strategic Objectives and Regime Status
* **Nuclear Denial:** The central stated goal remains ensuring Iran never acquires a nuclear weapon. Trump claimed previous strikes ("Operation Midnight Hammer") destroyed key facilities and that current operations have "checked the nuclear problem off the list."
* **Unintentional Regime Change:** Trump asserted that while regime change was not the official goal, it has occurred because the original leadership is "all dead." He described the successor group as "less radical" and "more reasonable."
* **Future Targets:** If negotiations fail, the President threatened to destroy Iran's entire electrical grid and its oil infrastructure, which has been intentionally spared thus far to allow for potential rebuilding.

## Energy Security and the Strait of Hormuz
* **Gas Prices:** Domestic gas prices have exceeded $4.00 per gallon. Trump dismissed this as a "short-term increase" caused by Iranian terror attacks on tankers, promising prices will "rapidly come back down" once the operation concludes.
* **U.S. Energy Independence:** Trump emphasized that the U.S. is the world's top oil and gas producer and "imports almost no oil through the Hormuz strait," suggesting the U.S. no longer needs to secure the waterway for its own sake.
* **Ultimatum to Allies:** The President demanded that countries dependent on Middle Eastern oil—specifically those that refused to join the war—must take the lead in protecting the Strait of Hormuz. 
    * **Direct Message:** He suggested allies "build up some delayed courage" and "just take" the strait themselves, as the U.S. military has already done the "hard part."

## Diplomatic and Domestic Context
* **NATO Tensions:** Before the speech, Trump reportedly threatened to exit NATO due to allies' refusal to join the war effort. While legally difficult, analysts note he could severely limit U.S. participation via executive order.
* **Public Opinion:** New polling indicates 60% of Americans disapprove of the war, and 67% believe the administration lacks a clear plan to resolve the conflict.
* **Negotiations vs. Escalation:** Reporters noted a contradiction in Trump's rhetoric: he claimed Iran is "begging" for a ceasefire while Iranian state media remains defiant and the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

## NASA Achievement: Artemis II
* **Lunar Milestone:** The briefing coincided with the successful launch of Artemis II, the first crewed mission to the moon in over 50 years.
* **Mission Details:** The crew (Wiseman, Glover, Koch, and Hansen) is on a 10-day mission to orbit the moon. This serves as a precursor to establishing a permanent lunar base and eventually reaching Mars.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "Tonight, Iran's Navy is gone. Their Air Force is in ruins. Their leaders—most of them, terrorist regime they led—are now dead." — **President Donald Trump**

> "We are going to hit them extremely hard over the next two to three weeks. We're going to bring them back to the stone ages where they belong." — **President Donald Trump**

> "I heard the president say tonight that those objectives had been met... What I did also hear was a threat. And that threat was to the countries around the world that depend on the oil... he was saying, we have the ability to walk away." — **Colonel Steve Ganyard, ABC News Military Analyst**

> "I listened very carefully... there was nothing new in that speech... it was almost an afterthought when he talked about the negotiations with the Iranians." — **Jonathan Karl, ABC News Chief Washington Correspondent**

briefings.title: LIVE: Trump addresses the nation on the Iran war | NBC News
briefings.tldr: President Trump declared a tactical military victory over Iran following one month of "Operation Epic Fury," claiming the regime’s navy and air force are destroyed, though he extended the expected timeline for completion by another two to three weeks.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump declared a tactical military victory over Iran following one month of "Operation Epic Fury," claiming the regime’s navy and air force are destroyed, though he extended the expected timeline for completion by another two to three weeks. Despite the President’s claims of a "new, more reasonable" Iranian regime and a pending return to low energy prices, analysts note that the Strait of Hormuz remains restricted and global oil markets reacted to the speech with price increases.

## Military Status and "Operation Epic Fury"
*   **Tactical Successes:** President Trump stated that after four weeks of conflict, the Iranian navy has been "absolutely destroyed," their air force is in ruins, and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has been decimated.
    *   **Nuclear Infrastructure:** The President highlighted "Operation Midnight Hammer," involving B-2 bombers that allegedly obliterated Iran’s primary nuclear facilities.
    *   **Casualties:** The President confirmed that 13 American service members have been killed in the conflict to date.
*   **Strategic Perspective:** NBC News military analyst Col. Steve Warren clarified that while the U.S. has achieved "tactical military victories" (sinking ships, degrading ballistic missiles), it is much harder to claim a "strategic victory" regarding long-term regional stability.
*   **Venezuela Reference:** Trump claimed a secondary military success in Venezuela, describing the U.S. as "joint venture partners" in oil production following a "quick, lethal, violent" intervention.

## Energy Independence and the Strait of Hormuz
*   **The "Tehran Tollbooth":** Correspondent Raf Sanchez reported that the Strait of Hormuz has slowed from 110 ships per day to roughly 5–10. Iran is reportedly forcing vessels into their waters and charging "tolls" of up to $2 million per passage.
*   **U.S. Economic Strategy:** Trump emphasized "drill baby drill" policies, asserting that the U.S. is now the top producer of oil and gas globally and is "totally independent" of Middle Eastern energy.
    *   **Allied Responsibility:** The President argued the U.S. has no domestic need for the Strait of Hormuz and suggested that countries dependent on that oil must "take the lead" in protecting and reopening the passage.
*   **Market Reaction:** Despite Trump’s assurance that gas prices will drop, Brent crude oil prices jumped by $4 per barrel during his 20-minute address, reflecting market skepticism regarding a swift resolution.

## Diplomacy and the "New Regime" Claims
*   **Regime Change Status:** Trump claimed that a "new group" is in power in Tehran following the deaths of original leaders, describing them as "less radical." 
    *   **Expert Skepticism:** NBC analysts noted there is "no evidence" of a truly new regime, pointing out that the son of the previous leader is in power and the underlying ideology remains unchanged.
*   **Diplomatic Overlooks:** Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian released a 1,000-word conciliatory letter in English ahead of the speech. However, experts noted Pezeshkian lacks real power in the Iranian system, especially after the death of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
*   **Negotiation Track:** While Trump mentioned ongoing discussions, he threatened to hit Iran’s electric generating plants "simultaneously" if a deal is not reached within the next 14 to 21 days.

## Domestic Context and Artemis 2
*   **Space Achievement:** The President opened his address by congratulating NASA on the successful launch of Artemis 2, noting the four astronauts will travel further than any humans in history.
*   **Inflation Discrepancy:** Trump claimed there is "no inflation" in the U.S.; however, NBC’s Brian Cheung corrected the record, noting government data shows prices rose 2.4% on a yearly basis. 
*   **Public Opinion:** Sources indicated the war is increasingly unpopular, with a majority of Americans disapproving of the military action as national gas prices exceed $4 per gallon.

## Notable Quotes

> "Never in the history of warfare has an enemy suffered such clear and devastating large-scale losses in a matter of weeks. Our enemies are losing and America... is winning and now winning bigger than ever before." 
> — **President Donald Trump**

> "If we define victory as accomplishing the military objectives that were initially laid out... it is a tactical military victory. Now, military objectives have to feed into a broader strategy... it would be a lot harder to say that there’s been a strategic victory tonight."
> — **Colonel Steve Warren**, NBC News Military Analyst

> "The countries of the world that do receive oil through the Hormuz Strait must take care of that passage, they must cherish it... Go to the Strait and just take it, protect it, use it for yourselves."
> — **President Donald Trump**

> "A lot of people here in the Middle East are asking to what extent is the President just creating his own reality when he says that the Iranians want a ceasefire and that it is a new government... over in Tehran."
> — **Raf Sanchez**, NBC News Correspondent

briefings.title: President Trump Addresses the Nation on Iran War
briefings.tldr: One month into "Operation Epic Fury," President Trump declared the near-total destruction of Iran’s military infrastructure and leadership, framing the conflict as a necessary "America First" action to permanently eliminate Iran’s nuclear ambitions and "conventional shield" of missiles and drones.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
One month into "Operation Epic Fury," President Trump declared the near-total destruction of Iran’s military infrastructure and leadership, framing the conflict as a necessary "America First" action to permanently eliminate Iran’s nuclear ambitions and "conventional shield" of missiles and drones.

## Military Progress and "Operation Epic Fury"
* **Status of Forces:** President Trump reported that after 32 days of conflict, Iran’s navy is "gone," its air force is in ruins, and the command structure of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has been decimated.
* **Targeting Leadership:** The President stated that most of the regime's original leaders are now dead, leading to a "less radical" provisional government.
* **Operation Midnight Hammer:** Trump highlighted a previous June strike where B-2 bombers "totally obliterated" key nuclear facilities to prevent the regime from reaching "weapons-grade" enrichment.
* **Conventional Shield:** Secretary of State Marco Rubio emphasized that the primary goal was destroying Iran’s massive stockpile of drones and missiles, which functioned as a shield to protect their nuclear program from international interference.

## Energy Independence and the Global Economy
* **Oil Production:** Trump asserted that the U.S. is now the #1 producer of oil and gas globally, producing more than Saudi Arabia and Russia combined through "drill, baby, drill" policies.
* **Venezuela Partnership:** The President claimed the U.S. military took control of Venezuela in a "quick, lethal" operation, turning the country into a "joint venture partner" to secure the world's second-largest oil reserves.
* **Strait of Hormuz:** 
    * **U.S. Stance:** Trump argued the U.S. is no longer dependent on the Strait for energy and suggested other nations must "build up some delayed courage" to protect their own shipping lanes.
    * **Economic Outlook:** Despite a short-term spike in gas prices and market volatility, Trump predicted a "roaring" economic recovery once the conflict concludes and the Strait "opens up naturally."

## Geopolitical Strategy and NATO
* **The "Axis of Aggressors":** Matthew Kroenig (Atlantic Council) identified a dangerous "World War III" style interlinkage between China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea, noting that China remains the most capable adversary the U.S. has ever faced.
* **NATO Friction:** Trump expressed frustration with European allies for their reluctance to support Middle Eastern operations. While reports suggested a potential U.S. withdrawal from NATO, Kroenig noted the alliance remains a major asset and highlighted Secretary General Mark Rutte’s upcoming "Trump whisperer" visit to Washington.
* **Regional Allies:** The administration reaffirmed strong support for Israel, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the UAE, Kuwait, and Bahrain as key partners in the "decapitation" of the Iranian threat.

## Domestic and International Reaction
* **Supportive Views:** Callers praised Trump’s "peace through strength" approach and his "proactive" defense of American interests, with some students viewing the administration as securing the future for the next generation.
* **Critical Opposition:**
    * **Legal Concerns:** Critics and Democratic leaders (e.g., Hakeem Jeffries, Chris Van Hollen) labeled the war "reckless," "unmoored," and a "war of choice" conducted without a formal declaration from Congress.
    * **Israel Influence:** Several independent and Republican callers questioned if the U.S. was acting as a "proxy for Israel" and expressed disappointment over the shift away from a "no new wars" campaign promise.

briefings.title: The Private Credit Reckoning is Coming: Executives Are Mistaking Luck For Genius | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: Private credit executives are exhibiting the same systemic arrogance seen on Wall Street prior to the 2008 financial crisis, mistaking a 17-year absence of a credit cycle for personal genius while hiding significant risks through "data massaging."
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Private credit executives are exhibiting the same systemic arrogance seen on Wall Street prior to the 2008 financial crisis, mistaking a 17-year absence of a credit cycle for personal genius while hiding significant risks through "data massaging."

## Geopolitical Volatility and Market Sentiment
* **The Iran War Variable:** Steve Eisman identifies the war as the primary driver of market movement, noting that the S&P 500 and Nasdaq ended Q1 down 4.6% and 7.1% respectively, largely due to conflict-related fears.
* **Trump’s Strategy:** Contradictory headlines are causing market whiplash. While the *Wall Street Journal* reported Trump might end the war without reopening the Strait of Hormuz, Trump’s own social media statements suggest a more aggressive stance, demanding other nations "go get your own oil."
* **Investment Difficulty:** Eisman expresses skepticism that Trump would accept a closed Strait, as it would be viewed as a defeat, making current investment decisions difficult as the market "trades headlines."

## The "Data Massaging" of Private Credit
* **Understated Software Exposure:** A recent *Wall Street Journal* analysis suggests private credit funds are intentionally misclassifying loans to make software exposure appear smaller than it is (often labeling software companies as "Healthcare" or other sectors they serve).
* **Significant Discrepancies:** Four major funds showed a marked difference between reported and actual software exposure:
    * **Blue Owl Credit Income Fund:** Reported 11.6%; Actual ~21%.
    * **Blackstone (BCRED):** Reported 25.7%; Actual ~33%.
    * **Ares Capital Corp:** Reported 23.8%; Actual ~30%.
    * **Apollo Debt Solutions Fund:** Reported 13.6%; Actual ~16%.
* **The AI Threat:** If AI disrupts the software sector, these massive, opaque exposures could lead to "ugly" losses that bleed into banks, pension funds, and life insurance companies.

## Psychological Herd Mentality in Hedge Funds
* **Counterintuitive Market Moves:** Despite war and inflation—factors that usually drive gold prices up—gold has declined 10%. 
* **Forced Liquidation:** Eisman attributes this to "herd mentality" among major funds (Citadel, Millennium, etc.). These funds held similar trades betting on lower rates and higher gold. When interest rate bets went wrong, risk managers forced them to sell their gold positions to cover losses, driving the price down.

## Structural Risks: Mistaking Luck for Genius
* **The "Lack of Cycle" Delusion:** Eisman argues that because there hasn't been a significant credit cycle in 17 years, current lending executives have forgotten that the "cost of goods sold" in lending is future losses.
* **Arrogance Parallel to 2008:** Just as GFC-era bankers mistook high leverage for genius, today’s private credit executives mistake a long period of low defaults for superior underwriting.
* **Opaqueness:** Because these funds price their own loan portfolios (marking their own cards), the industry lacks the transparency required to maintain investor trust during a downturn.

## Mailbag: GameStop and Fund Structures
* **GameStop (GME) Analysis:** Eisman rejects the idea that GME is a "value stock." While the company has $2.2 billion in net cash, its core retail business is terminal. He views Michael Burry’s thesis—that GME could use cash for acquisitions—as a "pipe dream" with too many variables.
* **Private Funds vs. BDCs:** 
    * **BDCs (e.g., OCSL):** Publicly listed, regulated by the SEC, limited to 2:1 leverage, and must distribute 90% of income.
    * **Private Vehicles (e.g., BCRED):** Restricted to "qualified purchasers," they avoid SEC registration, face no leverage limits, and have no public reporting requirements, making them more attractive to managers seeking higher fees and less oversight.

> "An entire generation of private credit executives have mistaken a lack of a credit cycle for genius... When private credit eventually blows up, it's going to be a shock to the industry's executives. Just like the GFC was a shock to Wall Street executives." — **Steve Eisman**

> "Private credit's exposure to software is so large that the industry wants to massage the data to make it seem smaller... Once the trust is broken, it's hard to restore." — **Steve Eisman**

> "What makes lending a unique business is that the cost of goods sold is unknown at point of sale. In the case of lending, the cost of goods sold is losses, and those losses always occur sometime in the future." — **Steve Eisman**

people.name: Jacob Walthour

briefings.tldr: Jacob Walthour, CEO of Blueprint Capital Advisors, emphasizes a strategic shift toward energy and AI infrastructure while warning of liquidity "cracks" in private credit, ultimately advocating for aggressive self-investment to navigate AI-driven career displacement.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Jacob Walthour, CEO of Blueprint Capital Advisors, emphasizes a strategic shift toward energy and AI infrastructure while warning of liquidity "cracks" in private credit, ultimately advocating for aggressive self-investment to navigate AI-driven career displacement.

## Investment Strategy & Market Outlook
*   **Top Stock Pick (Nvidia):** Walthour identifies Nvidia as the most accessible public play for the AI boom, as many other high-growth AI platforms remain in private venture capital stages.
*   **The Energy Bull Case:** High conviction in the energy sector due to the massive power demands of data centers, AI infrastructure, and Bitcoin mining. 
    *   **Energy Consumption:** One Bitcoin requires as much energy to produce as a single household consumes over 13 years.
    *   **Key Companies:** Mentions Williams, Constellation, and NextEra as firms effectively investing in necessary infrastructure.
*   **Private Credit Warning:** Walthour warns of "cracks" in the private credit market following a decade of expansion.
    *   **Liquidity Mismatch:** Investors are seeking redemptions that some large managers (citing Blue Owl as an example) are struggling to meet.
    *   **Tech Overexposure:** He critiques the "miscalculated risk" of lending to tech companies that have failed to produce profits for 15–20 years.

## Career Development & Financial Literacy
*   **The $10,000 Investment:** If given $10,000 today, Walthour advises investing it in **personal training and AI certifications** (e.g., from MIT or Harvard) to prevent being displaced by technological innovation.
*   **Portfolio Philosophy:** He differentiates between two distinct wealth stages:
    *   **The "Get Rich" Portfolio:** Aimed at younger investors; focuses on high risk and maximum return.
    *   **The "Stay Rich" Portfolio:** Aimed at older investors; prioritizes capital preservation and safety.
*   **The Power of Persistence:** Walthour recounts calling a contact at Lehman Brothers 14 times to secure his first internship, emphasizing that "iron sharpens iron" and the importance of mentorship in the "Wall Street game."

## AI & Technological Disruption
*   **Software Sector Risk:** There is significant market suspicion that AI will "disintermediate" traditional software companies, leading to sell-offs even in companies with record performance.
*   **Operational Efficiency:** Walthour uses ChatGPT as a research and proofreading tool to shorten his research process. 
    *   **The "75% Rule":** He uses AI to get 75% of the answers he needs in 35 seconds, making him "smarter faster" while acknowledging the need for human fact-checking.

## Blueprint Capital Advisors & Social Impact
*   **Firm Profile:** A Newark-based investment management firm with approximately $2 billion in total assets ($360 million discretionary; $1.36 billion non-discretionary as of March 2025).
*   **Core Focus:** Primarily focused on private credit and private equity (including venture capital, growth, and buyouts).
*   **"People Over Profits":** Walthour emphasizes the "ripple effect" of entrepreneurship, where firm success allows for recycling capital back into the community to support local organizations and economic solidification for families of color.
*   **The Power 100:** An initiative launched by Walthour to amplify "Black excellence" in asset management and create a resilient ecosystem against narratives that dismiss the contributions of women and people of color.

## Notable Quotes
> "There's a 'get rich' portfolio and then there's a 'stay rich' portfolio. Younger people, the get-rich portfolio. Older people, stay-rich portfolio." — **Jacob Walthour**

> "In our business, when the tide goes out, you see who's swimming naked. The tide is going out. Now you're starting to see who's overexposed to technology in their private credit portfolios." — **Jacob Walthour**

> "I think the biggest investment people can make today is in themselves... If you are worried about AI, and we all should be... you need to be investing in understanding those technologies and figuring out from a career perspective whether you're going to get displaced." — **Jacob Walthour**

briefings.title: Your 'first time' can shape democracy: the psychology of voting

people.name: Michael Bruter
people.role: Director, Electoral Psychology Observatory at LSE

briefings.tldr: Democratic participation is an intimate, relational experience rather than a purely rational one; the physical environment of voting and the "experiential" nature of a citizen’s first two elections are the primary determinants of lifelong engagement and political moderation.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Democratic participation is an intimate, relational experience rather than a purely rational one; the physical environment of voting and the "experiential" nature of a citizen’s first two elections are the primary determinants of lifelong engagement and political moderation.

## The Impact of "Electoral Ergonomics"
The physical and social environment in which a vote is cast significantly influences voter behavior and psychological state.

*   **Polling Station vs. Remote Voting:** Voting in person fosters a sense of collective responsibility and "societal projection." 
    *   **Extremism Risk:** Research indicates that 18-to-24-year-olds are twice as likely to vote for extremist parties when voting remotely (e.g., at a kitchen table) compared to voting in a communal polling station.
*   **Environmental Design:** Most polling stations are repurposed schools or churches, but intentional design—such as soundproofing or specific booth views—can change how a voter relates to the act of voting.
*   **Empathic Displacement:** In a physical polling environment, voters are more likely to consider how their individual action interacts with the needs of the broader community.

## The Critical Window of the First Vote
A citizen's early experience with democracy dictates their long-term participation habits.

*   **Lifelong Participation:** If an individual votes in one of their first two eligible elections, they are likely to become a lifelong participant. If these opportunities are missed, it is significantly harder to bring them into the democratic process later.
*   **The "First Time" Milestone:** Many young people experience their first vote as a deeply intimate milestone, comparing it to a first kiss or a first sexual experience rather than a mundane task like getting a driver’s license.
*   **Lowering the Voting Age:** Professor Bruter suggests that lowering the voting age to 16 can be effective because young people at that age are more willing to learn and discuss the process with family and teachers than they are at 18 or 19.

## Hostility vs. Polarization
While political discourse often focuses on polarization, the psychological reality for younger generations is a distinct "hostility."

*   **Defining Hostility:** Young voters are not necessarily "polarized" (deeply loyal to one camp); instead, they are often hostile toward everyone, including those who vote for the same candidates.
*   **Individual Sovereignty:** Younger voters reject being "pigeonholed" into groups. They view themselves as unique, independent thinkers who want to make an individual contribution to a collective movement.
*   **Inefficacy of Deliberative Democracy:** Because young people value their individuality so highly, traditional "deliberative democracy" tools often fail to reduce their hostility.

## The "Negative Mirror Perception" Problem
Social friction across generations is driven less by actual dislike and more by the false assumption of being disliked.

*   **Mirror Perceptions:** Most generations report liking and respecting each other. However, they suffer from "negative mirror perceptions"—the belief that the other generation views them with indifference, prejudice, aggression, or humiliation.
*   **Disinhibiting Conflict:** When people believe they are being judged or hated by another group, they feel justified in "defending" themselves, which leads to a cycle of alienation.
*   **The Solution of Real-Life Dialogue:** The most effective way to counter deepfakes, AI manipulation, and social hostility is to facilitate real-life, empathetic conversations between people with differing viewpoints.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "People voting in one of the first two elections of their lives will make them lifelong participants. If we miss one of those first two opportunities, it's going to be very difficult to bring them back to democracy." — **Professor Michael Bruter**

> "Young people are not polarized; they are hostile. And what it means is that they're very negative towards people who vote differently from them, but they're almost as negative towards people who vote for the same political parties." — **Professor Michael Bruter**

> "If [young people] vote remotely, from their kitchen table, they are twice more likely to vote for extremist parties than if they go to a polling station." — **Professor Michael Bruter**

> "We need to stop assuming that people are more biased than us, more selfish than us, more apathetic than us. We need to give them the credit that they might be as good and well-intending as we are." — **Professor Michael Bruter**
